reproduction_target: Reproduce, from the raw Illumina BCL/FASTQ of the ten single-cell/single-nucleus libraries (two placental donors x five modalities: Fresh_droplet_PolyA, Fixed_droplet_Probe, FFPE_droplet_Probe, Nuclei_droplet_PolyA, Fixed_in-situ_PolyA) plus the Xenium in situ spatial transcriptomics run on a third placenta, the count matrices (cellranger mkfastq/multi and Parse split-pipe all/comb against GRCh38-2020-A), the CellBender 0.2.0 ambient-RNA correction, the Seurat 5.1.0 quality filtering / integration / Louvain clustering / manual marker-based two-level cell type annotation, and then the five reported result families: (i) sensitivity and cell-capture-efficiency and background metrics (Figure 2), (ii) immune / non-immune and granular cell type proportions per modality against the iST reference (Figure 3), (iii) pseudobulked STB PCA and UMAP (Figure 4a,b), (iv) the STB and NK/T pseudobulk cross-modality Pearson correlation matrix and the LINC/RP/MIR percentage-of-counts distributions (Figure 4c,d), and (v) the inter-modality overlap of the top and bottom 10/25/50/100 Wilcoxon DEGs between the two biological replicates (Figure 5a). Patient recruitment and consent, placental sampling and storage, enzymatic/mechanical dissociation and MACS dead-cell removal, cell fixation, nuclei isolation, FFPE section dissociation, library preparation, NovaSeq 6000 sequencing and the Xenium instrument run are wet-lab and out of scope (W).
granularity_note: One step per named tool/analysis invocation in the MATERIAL AND METHODS section of the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML. 16 computational steps, 8 wet-lab steps. The JATS XML returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch but 200 to curl with a browser user-agent (77590 bytes); the title phrase 'difficult human tissue: the placenta' was confirmed present before scoring, so this is the correct paper. The article body, back matter (Acknowledgements, Author Contributions, Conflict of Interest, Funding, References) and the v1 landing HTML were all read. There is NO Data Availability section and NO Code Availability section anywhere in the article: a case-insensitive grep of the full XML for github|gitlab|bitbucket|zenodo|figshare|software heritage|GSE[0-9]+|PRJ[EDN][A-Z][0-9]+|SRP[0-9]+|E-MTAB-[0-9]+|EGA[SD][0-9]+|dbGaP|phs[0-9]+|data availability|code availability|availability of data|accession|deposited|repositor returned ZERO hits, and the same grep over the v1 landing HTML also returned zero hits. Stage-1 prose triage only: no code was read (there is none to read) and nothing was executed.

steps.label: Recruitment of 3 pregnant women at University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust under REC 17/SC/0432 (singleton pregnancy, iatrogenic preterm C-section before 37 weeks; stated exclusions), and placental sampling within 30 minutes of delivery: two DPBS washes, three adjacent 2cm x 2cm samples from the midpoint between cord insertion and placental edge, allocated to cold HypoThermosol FRS (<=24 h, 4 degrees C), isopentane/dry-ice snap freezing with OCT embedding at -80 degrees C, and formalin saline for FFPE blocks

Enzymatic and mechanical dissociation of the HypoThermosol-stored samples: mincing in C-Tubes, 10 ml Accutase, gentleMACS Octo dissociator with an undisclosed custom protocol, stacked 100 um / 70 um strainers, 300 RCF spins, Red Cell Lysis buffer (10 min RT), washes in DMEM 10% FBS

Dead cell removal by MACS: Dead Cell Removal MicroBeads (15 min RT), LS columns pre-rinsed with 1x Binding Buffer, elution and resuspension in DMEM 10% FBS; final suspension split three ways per donor
Cell fixation of the two non-fresh aliquots: Parse Biosciences Evercode Cell Fixation v2 User Manual v2.3, and 10X Genomics demonstrated protocol CG000478 rev D
Nuclei isolation from snap-frozen OCT-embedded placenta: five 25 um cryosections on a Bright OTF5000 cryostat, Chromium Nuclei Isolation Kit (10X Genomics 1000494) per user guide CG000505
FFPE block dissociation: five 25 um microtome sections dissociated per 10X Genomics demonstrated protocol CG000632 revD

Cell/nuclei counting by Acridine Orange / Propidium Iodide stain on a Logos Biosystems Luna FL, and library generation per the (figure-only) Table 1 specifications using 10X Genomics Next GEM Single-cell 5' v2, Parse Biosciences Evercode WT Mini v2, and 10X Genomics Chromium Fixed RNA Profiling Reagent Kit; sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000 with S4 200-cycle v1.5 kits above the minimum recommended depth per library type

In situ spatial transcriptomics run: 8 um placental section (third donor, 35 weeks) on the 10X Genomics Xenium Analyser (cat nos 1000460, 1000487, 1000461) with the Xenium Human Multi-Tissue and Cancer Panel (1000626) plus a Xenium Add-on Custom 51-to-100 Gene Panel (1000651), following CG000581 and user guides CG000582 / CG000584; the custom panel gene selection was derived from DEGs in STB and CTB from a cited prior study
Droplet libraries: conversion of raw BCL files to FASTQ with cellranger 'mkfastq'. No Cell Ranger version, no sample sheet, no mkfastq arguments are given

Droplet libraries: alignment to the GRCh38-2020-A human reference (GENCODE v32 / Ensembl 98, 10X Genomics distribution) and per-library unique-transcript matrix generation with cellranger 'multi'. The reference build is pinned exactly; the Cell Ranger version and the multi config CSV (feature reference, probe set CSV for the Fixed RNA Profiling libraries, expected cells, chemistry, force-cells) are not given

Droplet libraries: ambient-RNA correction and cell-containing vs empty droplet classification with CellBender 0.2.0, run per library. No parameters are given (--expected-cells, --total-droplets-included, --fpr, --epochs, --learning-rate, --model) and no random seed is stated, although CellBender inference is stochastic; the 'fraction counts removed from cells' metric reported in Figure 2c is taken from this step's output
In situ (Parse Evercode) libraries: conversion of raw BCL files to FASTQ with bcl2fastq (spelled 'bcl2fatsq' in the Methods). No bcl2fastq version, no sample sheet, no arguments

In situ (Parse Evercode) libraries: alignment to the same GRCh38-2020-A reference (GENCODE v32 / Ensembl 98, 10X Genomics distribution, deliberately reused to keep gene detection comparable across modalities) and matrix generation with split-pipe 'all' and 'comb'. The reference build and the two subcommands are named; the split-pipe version, the --chemistry / --kit / sublibrary definitions and all other arguments are not given

In situ libraries: merging of the unfiltered per-library matrices with Seurat 5.1.0 and export to a .h5ad object so that ambient RNA can be estimated across the merged object. The merge strategy, the .h5ad conversion route (SeuratDisk / sceasy / anndata) and its version are not stated

In situ libraries: ambient-RNA correction of the merged .h5ad object with CellBender 0.2.0. Again no parameters and no seed; note the asymmetry with C3 (per-library for droplet, merged for in situ), which is stated but not justified numerically

Quality filtering of single-cell / single-nucleus libraries with Seurat 5.1.0: exclude cells with detected genes < 400 or > 6,000, transcript counts > 17,500, mitochondrial read percentage > 10%, and haemoglobin gene percentage > 0.25%. All four thresholds are stated explicitly, but the mitochondrial and haemoglobin gene patterns/lists used to compute the percentages are not given

iST branch: construction of Seurat objects from the pre-processed data files generated by the Xenium instrument on-board analysis software, filtering out cells with 0 transcript counts. The Xenium Onboard Analysis / Xenium Ranger software version is not stated and its outputs are instrument-produced, so this step consumes an artifact that cannot be regenerated off-instrument

Data integration using 'a standard workflow': normalisation ('LogNormalise', i.e. Seurat LogNormalize) and scaling ('ScaleData') for the single-cell / single-nuclei libraries, and 'SCTransform' for the iST data. Libraries of each modality were integrated separately, except FFPE_droplet_Probe and Fixed_droplet_Probe which were processed together. The integration method itself (CCA / RPCA / Harmony / merge-only), scale.factor, nfeatures, vars.to.regress and the number of integration anchors are not named

Highly variable gene selection, principal component analysis, k-nearest-neighbour graph construction and graph-based Louvain community detection. No nfeatures, no number of PCs, no k.param, no clustering resolution and no random seed are given, and the whole clustering pipeline is re-run after subsetting (see C12)

Two-level cell type annotation from the expression of 'manually curated genes from the literature': first into immune vs non-immune, then re-clustering each subset for higher granularity (STB, CTB, EVT, NK/T, Hofbauer, myofibroblasts, etc.). Doublet clusters were identified by a mixed profile of mutually exclusive marker genes and excluded. The marker gene panel is not provided, the literature sources for it are not enumerated, and doublet identification is manual and judgement-based (no DoubletFinder/scDblFinder run)

Merging of the filtered and annotated libraries with Seurat 5.1.0, consistency check of annotations, and computation of the reported summary metrics: cell type proportions per modality at both annotation levels (Figure 3), percentage of counts per cell for the Long Intergenic Non-Coding (LINC), Ribosomal Protein (RP) and Micro RNA (MIR) gene classes (Figure 4d), and cells surviving QC and doublet filtration as a percentage of cells input at sample processing (Figure 2b). The gene lists defining LINC / RP / MIR (prefix regex vs GENCODE biotype) are not given, and the per-library input cell counts live only in the figure-image Table 1

STB subsetting, pseudobulking by sample with Seurat 'AggregateExpression', 'RunPCA' on the top 2,000 most variable genes per library with npcs=8, and 'RunUMAP' on the top 5 principal components (Figure 4a,b; PC1 60.3% and PC2 23.9% of variance). Parameters are unusually complete for this paper; the UMAP arguments (n.neighbors, min.dist, seed) and the pseudobulk normalisation applied before PCA are still unstated

Pseudobulking of STB and NK/T cells per cell type and modality with 'AggregateExpression', subsetting the non-probe-based modalities to the genes present in the probe sets, and computing a correlation matrix from the normalised transcript counts (Pearson coefficients 0.8-0.94 reported in Figure 4c). The probe-set gene lists (10X Chromium Fixed RNA Profiling human transcriptome probe set, version and CSV) are not deposited or version-named, and the normalisation applied to the pseudobulk counts before correlation is not stated

Inter-method differential gene expression: STB subsetting, pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests ('FindMarkers') between the two biological replicates within each modality, retention of DEGs with adjusted p < 0.05, ranking by descending log2 fold change, then computation of the overlap ratio of the top 10/25/50/100 and bottom 10/25/50/100 DEGs across modality pairs (Figure 5a). Test, significance cutoff, ranking rule and the four overlap depths are all stated; logfc.threshold, min.pct, the multiple-testing method behind 'adjusted p value', and the exact definition of 'ratio of overlap' are not

headline.static_readiness: 0/16 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; there is no declared environment at all to statically validate - the paper ships no lockfile, no container, no conda environment, no requirements file and no sessionInfo, only two exact in-prose version strings (CellBender 0.2.0, Seurat 5.1.0). n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0. Under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/16 (0%) readiness upper bound at stage 1: (n_R + n_RI) / |S| = (0 + 0) / 16. The binding constraints are the data axis AND the code axis, both 0 on every computational step, and both for the same reason: this preprint contains no Data Availability statement and no Code Availability statement of any kind. A case-insensitive grep of the complete JATS XML for github|gitlab|bitbucket|zenodo|figshare|software heritage|GSE|PRJEB/PRJNA/PRJDB|SRP|E-MTAB|EGAS/EGAD|dbGaP|phs|data availability|code availability|availability of data|accession|deposited|repositor returned ZERO hits, as did the same grep over the v1 landing page. No FASTQ, no count matrix, no CellBender-corrected matrix, no annotated Seurat object, no DEG table and no Xenium output is retrievable, and no analysis script exists to inspect. Method reporting is otherwise mid-range for this genre: two tools carry exact version pins, the reference genome build is pinned exactly (GRCh38-2020-A / GENCODE v32 / Ensembl 98) and four steps (C8, C14, C16, and partially C10) state their parameters well, so the paper would move to RI on most steps if the libraries were deposited under a study accession and the analysis scripts were released - but it cannot move above RI without environment capture. Note additionally that the study is human placental tissue under REC 17/SC/0432, so the raw data would legitimately belong in a controlled-access archive (EGA/dbGaP); controlled access is NOT penalised by this rubric, but no accession and no data access committee route are stated, so data = 0 rather than 2.
headline.coverage: computational coverage |S| / (|S| + |W|) = 16 / 24 = 67%; 8 wet-lab steps (recruitment and sampling, dissociation, MACS dead-cell removal, cell fixation, nuclei isolation, FFPE dissociation, library prep and NovaSeq sequencing, Xenium instrument run) scored OOS

gaps.where: whole article - there is no Data Availability and no Code Availability section; affects every computational step C1-C16
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited, linked or mentioned. The article's back matter contains only Acknowledgements, Author Contributions, Conflict of Interest, Funding and References; there is no availability statement of any kind. A case-insensitive grep of the full JATS XML for github|gitlab|bitbucket|zenodo|figshare|software heritage|data availability|code availability|availability of data|accession|deposited|repositor returned zero hits, and the identical grep over the bioRxiv v1 landing HTML also returned zero hits. Every result in the paper (cell type proportions, PCA/UMAP, correlation matrices, LINC/RP/MIR percentages, DEG overlap matrices) is produced by unreleased Seurat/R and CellBender/Python code. This sets code = 0 on all 16 computational steps.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis code (the cellranger multi config CSVs, the split-pipe invocation, the CellBender command lines, and the Seurat scripts that produce Figures 2-5) in a public repository and cite it by tag or archival DOI in a Code Availability statement.

gaps.missing: Because no repository exists, all analysis code is private by default. The paper does not state that code is available on request either, so there is not even a documented human route to it. Two steps in particular are irrecoverable from prose alone: the manual marker-based two-level annotation and manual doublet-cluster exclusion (C12), and the 'ratio of overlap' computation over the top/bottom 10/25/50/100 DEGs (C16), whose exact definition (intersection over union? intersection over k? symmetric?) determines every value in Figure 5a.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the annotation notebook including the marker gene panel, and the overlap-ratio function, so the two judgement-heavy steps become inspectable.

gaps.where: C1-C16 - no dataset is deposited, and no sample-to-library mapping is released outside a figure-image table
gaps.missing: No sequencing data, count matrix or processed object is deposited anywhere. No GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress, EGA, dbGaP, figshare or Zenodo identifier appears in the article or on the landing page. The ten single-cell/single-nucleus libraries (2 donors x 5 modalities) and the Xenium run are referred to only by modality nickname (Fresh_droplet_PolyA, Fixed_droplet_Probe, FFPE_droplet_Probe, Nuclei_droplet_PolyA, Fixed_in-situ_PolyA), and the per-library specifications - including the input cell counts that form the denominator of the Figure 2b capture-efficiency metric - exist only inside the figure-image Table 1, which is not machine-readable. This sets data = 0 on all 16 computational steps and is the single dominant blocker of the assessment.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw reads under a study accession (controlled-access EGA or dbGaP is fully acceptable under this rubric given REC 17/SC/0432, provided the accession resolves and the data access route is documented), deposit the CellBender-corrected and annotated matrices under GEO or Zenodo, and publish Table 1 as a machine-readable supplementary table with an explicit library-to-accession mapping.

gaps.where: C1, C2 (Cell Ranger), C4 (bcl2fastq), C5 (split-pipe), C9 (Xenium on-board analysis software); and environment closure for all of C1-C16
gaps.missing: Four of the six distinct tools used carry no version string at all. Cell Ranger is named only as 'cellranger' for both mkfastq and multi - a material omission, because Cell Ranger 6.x/7.x/8.x differ in cell calling, intronic-read handling and Fixed RNA Profiling probe handling, all of which directly affect the sensitivity and cell-recovery metrics that are this paper's headline result. split-pipe (Parse Biosciences) has no version despite the Evercode kit chemistry being explicitly at issue in the paper's central claim about combinatorial indexing. bcl2fastq and the Xenium Onboard Analysis pipeline are likewise unpinned. Only CellBender 0.2.0 and Seurat 5.1.0 are pinned exactly. Separately, exact prose pins do not constitute environment closure: no lockfile, no container digest, no conda environment YAML, no requirements.txt, no renv.lock and no R sessionInfo is provided, and no R or Python interpreter version is stated. The version axis is therefore capped at 1 for every step at stage 1, and at 0 for the four unversioned-tool steps.
gaps.how_to_close: State the Cell Ranger, split-pipe, bcl2fastq and Xenium Onboard Analysis version strings, and ship a conda-lock / renv.lock / container digest covering the R and Python environments so the version axis can reach 2.

gaps.where: C3, C7 (CellBender), C10, C11 (integration and clustering), C12 (annotation), C13 (gene class definitions), C15 (correlation)
gaps.missing: Several steps are described at a level that does not determine the computation. CellBender is run twice with no arguments at all, yet its output ('fraction counts removed from cells') is reported as a headline metric in Figure 2c. Integration is 'a standard workflow' with the integration method itself unnamed. Clustering states neither the number of HVGs, nor the number of PCs, nor k, nor the Louvain resolution, and the pipeline is re-run after subsetting with unstated (possibly different) settings. The marker gene panel behind the two-level annotation is 'manually curated genes from the literature' with no list and no citations enumerated. The LINC / RP / MIR gene classes central to Figure 4d are named but not defined (symbol-prefix regex versus GENCODE biotype gives materially different gene sets, particularly for MIR). The pseudobulk normalisation applied before the Pearson correlation in C15 is not stated.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full command lines and the R script, plus supplementary tables containing the marker gene panel, the LINC/RP/MIR gene lists, and the probe-set-intersected gene list used in C15.

gaps.where: C3, C7 (CellBender variational inference), C11 (UMAP and Louvain), C14 (RunPCA/RunUMAP)
gaps.missing: No random seed is stated anywhere in the Methods. CellBender's variational inference, the Louvain community detection, and UMAP are all stochastic; without a seed, cluster membership, cluster count and the UMAP embedding in Figures 3a and 4b can only be matched distributionally, not exactly. This caps these steps at RI even in the counterfactual where data, code and environment were all released.
gaps.how_to_close: Set and report seeds (set.seed in R, --seed/torch seed for CellBender), or state the tolerance within which the reported clustering is stable.

gaps.where: C2, C5 (GRCh38-2020-A reference), C2/C15 (10X Fixed RNA Profiling probe set), C9/W8 (Xenium panels)
gaps.missing: Mixed. The one strongly pinned external resource is the alignment reference: 'GRCh38-2020-A human reference genome (GENCODE v32/Ensembl98 distributed by 10X Genomics)', which is an exactly identifiable 10X release and is deliberately reused across both the droplet and the Parse branches to keep gene detection comparable - this is good practice and should be credited. The unpinned ones are the vendor gene panels: the 10X Chromium Fixed RNA Profiling probe set is never named or versioned even though the entire probe-versus-polyA comparison, and the gene subsetting in C15, depend on exactly which genes it contains; the Xenium Human Multi-Tissue and Cancer Panel and the Add-on Custom 51-to-100 Gene Panel are given by catalogue number only, and the custom panel's gene list (derived from a prior study's STB/CTB DEGs) is not deposited. No workflow file was read at stage 1, so none of these fetches can be classified A/B/C.
gaps.how_to_close: State the probe set CSV name and version, and deposit the custom Xenium panel gene list as a supplementary table.

gaps.where: C1, C2 (Cell Ranger), C5 (split-pipe), C9 (Xenium Onboard Analysis)
gaps.missing: Three of the four count-matrix-generating tool chains are vendor software. Cell Ranger and split-pipe are freely downloadable but registration-gated and version-archived at the vendors' discretion, so an unnamed version may not be obtainable years later. The Xenium Onboard Analysis output consumed by C9 is produced on the instrument itself and cannot be regenerated off-instrument at all - the iST branch is therefore only reproducible from the deposited instrument outputs, which are not deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the vendor tool versions, and deposit the Xenium instrument output bundle (transcripts.parquet / cell_feature_matrix) rather than relying on the instrument being re-runnable.

gaps.missing: Patient recruitment and consent, placental sampling and the three storage arms, enzymatic/mechanical dissociation, MACS dead-cell removal, cell fixation, nuclei isolation from OCT sections, FFPE section dissociation, library preparation and NovaSeq 6000 sequencing, and the Xenium instrument run are wet-lab; excluded from |S| as OOS. Note for the human reviewer: this paper's own central claim is that sample processing and storage - i.e. the W layer - drives more of the observed variance than chemistry does, so the OOS split here excludes the variable the paper identifies as dominant. That is correct under the rubric (NASEM computational reproducibility only) but should be stated when this paper is summarised, and the gentleMACS 'custom protocol' in W2 is undisclosed, which would block wet-lab replication independently.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - out of scope for computational reproducibility. (For completeness of the wet-lab record, the gentleMACS Octo custom dissociation program and the figure-image Table 1 library specifications should be published as text.)
